target_customer: Consumers ordering restaurant food, restaurants, and delivery drivers (Dashers)
problem: Many restaurants had no delivery; DoorDash hired and managed its own drivers to deliver from restaurants that did not offer delivery.
business_model: Marketplace take rate from restaurants plus delivery fees

founders.name: Evan Moore
founders.background_notes: Left after about 17 months per search summary (Wikipedia); later at Khosla Ventures.

exit.reason: Priced at $102 per share on 2020-12-08, raising $3.37B (amount is capital raised, not valuation)

competitors.name: Seamless/GrubHub
competitors.what: Online ordering apps that route orders to restaurants that deliver themselves

competitors.name: Fluc
competitors.what: Similar delivery startup charging $5.95 per order with inflated menu prices

technical_complexity.rationale: Initial prototype was built in a day in February 2013 and orders were fulfilled manually by the founders; logistics software became harder at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Anyone could replicate in 2013; later density and network effects of a three-sided marketplace emerged but are not documented in the sources fetched.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents later added delivery; DoorDash still grew to an IPO in December 2020. Details of incumbent copying not sourced here.

market_need_then: Founders saw a Palo Alto macaroon shop owner turning down delivery orders; the prototype got its first order within half an hour (Palo Alto Delivery, Feb 2013); delivered about 50 restaurants by July 2013 and doubled deliveries in two weeks.

branding.name_origin: Launched as Palo Alto Delivery (domain cost under $10 per Xu); renamed DoorDash in June 2013; the replacement name had to be easy to spell, two syllables or less and have an available domain (account in a podcast summary).
branding.domain_note: PaloAltoDelivery.com bought for under $10 (2013); exact doordash.com domain later used (date and price not found).

identity.logo: Redesigned in 2014 per DoorDash's own post, with a later Character-agency identity using negative space
identity.visual_style: Red and white palette tied to speed and food

rebrands.why: Prototype name was local; scaling beyond Palo Alto
Sign of growing maturity per company post

brand_strength.rationale: Short, easy-to-spell name chosen deliberately; DoorDash became a category-leading consumer brand, but sources fetched give no direct evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: DoorDash started as a one-day prototype in Palo Alto in early 2013, joined YC in summer 2013, and grew by hiring its own drivers to serve restaurants that did not offer delivery, a gap that Seamless and GrubHub did not fill. It raised a $17.3M Series A from Sequoia in 2014, repeated rounds through 2020 (including a reported $400M at $16B in June 2020) and went public in December 2020 raising $3.37B. Execution and market growth carried it; no source here quantifies defensibility or incumbent copying.
notes: Only seed and Series A recorded; Preqin says five rounds raised $729M between 2013 and 2018, then Series D onward through a June 2020 $400M round at a reported $16B; these later rounds are from one source and not recorded individually, so coverage is partial. The seed round ($2.4M, Khosla, Sept/Oct 2013) comes from a Vator article and search snippets; no second outlet fetched. Series A figure appears in the TechCrunch URL slug and snippet; not fetched. Moore's departure after 17 months and his education come from Wikipedia via search summary; Wikipedia says Moore and Xu were GSB while other sources call all four 'Stanford GSB class students', so education is uncertain. Name origin of 'door dash' itself not found. Rename date June 2013 per Wikipedia and Vator. Outcome search done: IPO. IPO valuation estimates vary (about $38-39B).
